Direction: P1 -> P2. Provide governed intent, purpose, semantic references, authority/accountability context and design/use obligations for discovery, resolution, composition and realization.
Direction: P1 -> P3. Constrain typed Data processing, Information formation or Intelligence execution by applicable purpose, authority, policy, quality, lifecycle and safety context.
Direction: P1 -> P4. Provide purpose, identity/mandate, Product/use context and governing constraints required for exposure, access, consumption and integration.
Direction: P1 -> P5. Provide intended outcomes, value hypotheses, evaluation context and governing interpretation boundaries for later outcome/value assessment.
Direction: P2 -> P1. Return ambiguity, missing intent, semantic incompatibility, authority gaps or design constraints requiring P1 refinement.
Direction: P4 -> P1. Return access, entitlement, purpose or consumption-context issues requiring P1 clarification or reframing.
Direction: P5 -> P1. Return outcome, effectiveness, consumer feedback or value evidence that may require intent, objectives, authority context or Product design evolution.
Direction: P1 -> affected P2-P5. Propagate material change in governing purpose, authority, mandate or constraints to affected downstream responsibilities without rewriting historical occurrences.
Direction: P2 -> P3. Provide the governed realization/binding context required to instantiate or invoke the applicable typed P3 runtime responsibility.
Direction: P3 -> P2. Return runtime eligibility, readiness, binding, deployment, dependency or realization-state feedback required for correction or re-binding.
Direction: P2 -> P4. Provide typed candidate Product/capability resolution results and rationale for consumer evaluation, acquisition or access processing.
Direction: P4 -> P2. Return Product/Port availability, access, compatibility or provisioning constraints requiring substitution, re-resolution or realization change.
Direction: P2 -> P4. Hand off an eligible/published realization and its governed interface/Port context for exposure and consumer onboarding.
Direction: P2 -> P5. Provide realization, dependency, compatibility and change-impact context needed to interpret outcomes and evolution consequences.
Direction: P5 -> P2. Request governed reassessment, recompilation, re-binding, substitution or realization change based on outcome/evolution evidence.
Direction: P2 -> affected P3/P4/P5. Propagate material realization, dependency, Blueprint, binding or interface change to affected runtime, provision and outcome responsibilities.
Direction: P4 -> P3. Request or invoke typed Data processing, Information formation or Intelligence execution through a governed provision/consumption boundary.
Direction: P3 -> P4. Return typed runtime result, output, status or effect for governed exposure, consumption or downstream integration.
Direction: P3 -> P5. Supply runtime outcome/effectiveness evidence and execution context needed for outcome/value/evolution interpretation.
Direction: P4 -> P5. Supply governed consumption, usage, delivery and integration evidence for outcome, value and lifecycle interpretation.
Direction: P5 -> P4. Inform continued use, substitution, changed experience, consumer feedback or other consumption-path adjustment without directly redefining Product semantics.

Class: BC5. Principal jurisdiction outside HDIP: Decision engines, tool/action systems, transactional systems, physical/digital actuators and accountable human decision environments.

elements.definition: HDIP-CLA SHALL NOT incompatibly redefine concepts, relationships or invariants owned by GEDRM, GEARM, GEAIRM or other applicable semantic authorities.
Generic Product identity, Product Intrinsic Nature and Product qualification SHALL remain governed by BPS/PIN rather than inferred by HDIP.
Data Product, Information Product, AI Product and other Product-family qualification/classification SHALL remain with the applicable Product-family authority.

Authority used by HDIP SHALL be explicit for an applicable scope, role, purpose, lifecycle state and/or jurisdiction where those distinctions matter; platform participation SHALL NOT imply universal authority.
Co-location, shared storage, shared runtime, shared registry, shared UI or shared platform realization SHALL NOT by itself transfer semantic, Product, policy, decision or ownership authority.
Where HDIP needs a semantic concept not owned by HDIP, the gap SHALL be referred to or extended through the appropriate semantic authority rather than silently minted as platform semantics.
Authority, approval, entitlement, policy applicability or ownership SHALL NOT become automatically transitive merely because a dependency, composition or interaction crosses an HDIP boundary.
A canonical HDIP ABB or mandatory implementation responsibility SHALL be justified by explicit architectural responsibility; a noun, tool, service label or historical box alone is insufficient.
A future HDIP Plane SHALL represent a coherent logical responsibility grouping and SHALL NOT imply a mandatory system, deployment unit, network tier, team, organizational boundary or lifecycle step.
HDIP-CLA conformance SHALL NOT depend on centralized, federated, distributed, edge, embedded, provider-managed or hybrid deployment topology unless a narrower Profile explicitly requires it.
One implementation MAY realize responsibilities from several HDIP logical structures, and one HDIP responsibility MAY be distributed across several implementations.
GEDRA, GEARA and GEAIRA plane numbering, placement or lexical similarity SHALL NOT force one-to-one HDIP plane mapping.

A responsibility that is cross-cutting in an applicable source architecture SHALL NOT be silently localized into one future HDIP plane without explicit justification that preserves its cross-cutting obligations.

Compute, storage, networking, messaging, identity infrastructure, orchestration and other utility capabilities SHALL NOT acquire semantic, Product, governance or domain authority merely because they enable those responsibilities.

Every future canonical HDIP Plane, Overlay, ABB and material interaction SHALL trace to upstream responsibilities, explicit enterprise platform requirements and/or justified HDIP-specific coordination responsibilities.
Data, Information and Intelligence SHALL remain distinguishable architectural/semantic concerns even where one platform capability co-realizes responsibilities from more than one domain.
A Data-specific, Information-specific or Intelligence-specific construct SHALL NOT automatically generalize to the other domains through shared implementation or naming similarity.

Composition, generation, transformation, persistence, deployment, publication, registration, cataloguing, marketplace presence, API exposure, repeated use or consumption SHALL NOT by itself establish Product identity.
Co-realization of Data Products, Information Products and AI Products SHALL NOT collapse them into one HDIP-local Product family or type.

Using, depending on, containing, deriving from or invoking a Product/capability SHALL NOT by itself transfer its Product family, ontology type, ownership or authority to the dependent/composed result.

HDIP SHALL be able to support governed Data, Information or Intelligence capability use where Product qualification is not intended; Productization SHALL NOT be a mandatory gateway for every governed interaction.
Self-service SHALL operate inside applicable authority, policy, security, privacy, quality, evidence and lifecycle constraints; self-service SHALL NOT mean unrestricted infrastructure or data access.
Participant-declared intent, business semantics and accountable judgement SHALL remain distinguishable from platform resolution, compilation, provisioning and automation.
HDIP automation SHALL NOT transfer Product ownership, Data authority, policy authority or decision accountability to the compiler/runtime merely because the platform performs most technical work.
Architecture/governance decisions requiring contextual or accountable judgement SHALL NOT be represented as machine-proven solely because metadata, telemetry, rules or model outputs exist.
PDEP SHALL remain the canonical HDIP Product Development and Evolution Process identity; historical SSPD terminology MAY remain only for traceability and SHALL NOT become a competing lifecycle.
PDEP G0 and PDEP Spec A MAY compress/group canonical stages for progressive disclosure, while PDEP Spec C SHALL remain synchronized with the canonical applicable detailed PDEP lifecycle.
Interactive flow players, diagrams, dashboards and experience projections SHALL NOT independently create lifecycle stages, authority, Product identity, ABBs or architecture semantics.

HPD, SYNCTX, resolved graphs, compiled governance bundles, compilation packs and similar HDIP-generated projections SHALL NOT override the authoritative semantics or governance sources they reference.

HDIP resolution/compilation SHALL NOT manufacture semantic relationships, Product identity, policy authority, joinability, provenance, dependencies or obligations from weak evidence or naming similarity.
ADS, Product, Schema, Policy, Capability and Blueprint registry responsibilities SHALL remain logically distinguishable even where one implementation realizes several of them.
Registration SHALL NOT by itself prove authoritative status, Product status, control effectiveness, semantic correctness, fitness or HDIP conformance.
Registry, Catalog and Marketplace responsibilities SHALL NOT be treated as architectural synonyms even when exposed through one user experience or implementation.
HDIP MAY consolidate registry implementation where operationally useful provided logical identities, ownership, contracts, lifecycle and authority boundaries remain distinguishable.
Material HDIP interactions SHOULD emit or retain applicable provenance, control, quality, observability and lifecycle evidence sufficient for later reconstruction and assessment.

Platform location, certification label, popularity, centralization, Product status or registry presence SHALL NOT be treated as universal proof of trust or fitness; trust assessment SHALL remain contextual and evidence-based.

elements.canonicalName: Missing evidence is not positive evidence
elements.definition: Missing, stale, inaccessible or materially ambiguous evidence SHALL NOT be interpreted as positive assurance.
Version identity, latest/newest status and governed currentness SHALL remain distinguishable; newest SHALL NOT automatically mean current or approved.

Later supersession, revocation, re-evaluation, upstream change, rollback or re-publication SHALL NOT silently rewrite which semantics, Product Version, policy/control, dependency, context or realization governed a historical occurrence.
Provenance and lineage SHALL support traceability but SHALL NOT by themselves prove correctness, authorization, control effectiveness, assurance or Fitness for Use.

A conformant HDIP architecture SHALL preserve the canonical identity and responsibility meaning of P1-P5, X1-X9, HDIP-FND and the M08 ABB catalogue; implementation grouping, view projection or profile specialization SHALL NOT silently redefine those canonical structures.

Material interactions SHALL preserve the applicable M12 Interaction Contract identity and obligations even when the participating responsibilities are co-located, embedded, distributed, provider-operated or implemented through a mechanism other than a network API.

Material crossings of an M13 Boundary Family SHALL preserve the applicable external authority, jurisdiction, currentness, evidence and failure obligations; physical co-location or shared-provider realization SHALL NOT erase the logical boundary.

Product or Product-Port access approval, entitlement or successful consumption SHALL NOT by itself authorize a downstream consequential Decision, Tool use, Digital Action or Physical Action where separate point-of-use authority is applicable.

PDEP, SSCF and CEP SHALL remain lifecycle/experience compositions and SHALL NOT be interpreted as mandatory synchronous runtime pipelines; an established governed runtime MAY reuse current lifecycle state until material change requires re-evaluation.

A concrete realization claiming HDIP alignment SHALL retain traceability from applicable canonical responsibilities, ABBs, Interaction Contracts, Boundary Families and Profile obligations to the Realization Units, human processes or adjacent systems that satisfy them.

HDIP conformance SHALL NOT by itself establish conformance to GEDRA, GEARA, GEAIRA, BPS/PIN, a Product-family specification, an external standard or provider certification, and conformance to an adjacent specification SHALL NOT by itself establish HDIP conformance.

An HDIP Profile MAY select, tighten, contextualize, specialize, narrow and extend the baseline for a bounded scope, but SHALL NOT weaken, waive or incompatibly redefine an applicable core invariant or transfer authority from an external semantic, Product, policy or Decision authority.
